title: Blood components & clotting
examples: What is the main job of platelets in blood?
How do red blood cells help us breathe?
What keeps the blood flowing and carrying nutrients?

explain.say: Today we learn about the parts of blood.

draw.text: Blood components: RBC, WBC, platelets, plasma

explain.say: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs.
White blood cells fight off germs and infections.
Platelets help to stop bleeding when you get a cut.
Plasma is the liquid part that carries everything around.
When you cut your finger, platelets form a plug to stop the blood loss.

faq.q: What is the main job of red blood cells?
faq.a: Their primary job is to transport oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
asks: What is oxygen transport in blood?

faq.q: Do all white blood cells fight germs in the same way?
faq.a: No, there are different types, like neutrophils and lymphocytes, each with a specific role in immunity.
asks: What types of WBCs are there?
How does the immune system use WBCs?

faq.q: Are platelets just tiny bits of blood?
faq.a: Yes, they are small cell fragments that are crucial for initiating the blood clotting process.
asks: What do platelets do when I bleed?

faq.q: What percentage of blood is plasma?
faq.a: Plasma is mostly water and acts as the medium that suspends all the blood cells.
asks: What is the liquid part of blood?

faq.q: If I lose too much blood, what happens?
faq.a: Losing too much blood means losing the necessary components, leading to shock and organ failure.
asks: What causes blood pressure to drop?

facts: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds to oxygen.
White blood cells are key components of the immune system.
Platelets help form a physical plug to prevent excessive blood loss.
Plasma contains dissolved proteins, electrolytes, and nutrients.

quiz.say: Which component is primarily responsible for transporting oxygen throughout the body?
quiz.why: RBCs contain haemoglobin, which is specifically designed to bind and carry oxygen from the lungs.

wrong.1: Plasma is the liquid part; while it carries dissolved gases, RBCs are the main carriers.
wrong.2: WBCs are focused on fighting infection, not oxygen transport.
wrong.3: Platelets are involved in stopping bleeding, which is a different function.

quiz.say: When a person is cut, which component immediately helps to seal the wound?
quiz.why: Platelets aggregate at the site of injury to form a temporary plug, which is the first step in clotting.

wrong.0: Plasma flows around the wound but does not form the initial physical seal.
wrong.1: RBCs are lost during bleeding; they do not form the plug themselves.
wrong.2: WBCs arrive later to clean up pathogens, not to stop the initial bleeding.

quiz.say: Plasma is mainly composed of which substance?
quiz.why: Plasma is mostly water, which acts as the solvent for carrying dissolved substances.

wrong.0: Haemoglobin is found inside the red blood cells, not dissolved in plasma.
wrong.1: Oxygen is carried by RBCs, not dissolved in the plasma in large amounts.
wrong.2: While antibodies are in plasma, the main component by volume is water.
